question.title: Tiling the Heat Map
question.content:
You are given a square integer matrix grid of heat readings, whose side length is a power of two. Compress it into a tree of Tile objects:

  • If every cell of a square holds the same reading, its tile has uniform set to true, heat set to that reading, and all four child fields null.
  • Otherwise, its tile has uniform set to false, heat set to the largest reading in the square, and the fields nw, ne, sw, and se set to the tiles of the four equal quarters of the square: top left, top right, bottom left, and bottom right.

Return the tile of the whole grid.

Test case format:

A tile tree is shown in level order, where each tile is [u, heat] with u being 1 if uniform is true and 0 otherwise. The children of a tile that is not uniform follow in the order nw, ne, sw, se. A uniform tile has no entries for its children.

 

Example 1:

Input: grid = [[6,6],[2,6]]
Output: [[0,6],[1,6],[1,6],[1,2],[1,6]]
Explanation: The readings differ, so the whole grid has four single cell tiles below it.

Example 2:

Input: grid = [[3,3,5,5],[3,3,5,5],[3,3,5,7],[3,3,5,5]]
Output: [[0,7],[1,3],[1,5],[1,3],[0,7],[1,5],[1,7],[1,5],[1,5]]
Explanation: Only the bottom right quarter is split again.

Example 3:

Input: grid = [[8]]
Output: [[1,8]]

 

Constraints:

  • grid.length == grid[i].length
  • grid.length == 2x where 0 <= x <= 6
  • 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 1000
